Solve Many Conditions in One Call

Source: R/solveODE.R
solveODEBatch.Rd

Integrates a compiled ODE model over several independent parameter sets (experimental conditions, or the subjects of a mixed-effects fit) inside a single .Call, using OpenMP where the toolchain provides it.

Usage

solveODEBatch(
  model,
  conditions,
  times = NULL,
  parms = NULL,
  tangent = NULL,
  hessian = NULL,
  fixed = NULL,
  forcings = NULL,
  abstol = 1e-06,
  reltol = 1e-06,
  maxattempts = 50L,
  maxsteps = 1000000L,
  hini = 0,
  roottol = 1e-06,
  maxroot = 1L,
  cores = NULL,
  traceFile = NULL,
  onFailure = c("stop", "warn", "silent"),
  cotangent = NULL,
  curvature = NULL,
  keepStore = FALSE,
  store = NULL,
  sensErrCon = TRUE,
  adjoint = NULL,
  maxOrder = NULL,
  stald = FALSE
)

Arguments

model

A model handle from cppODE() or cvode().

conditions

A named or unnamed list of per-condition argument lists. Recognized names are times, parms, tangent, hessian, cotangent, curvature, fixed, forcings, abstol, reltol, maxattempts, maxsteps, hini, roottol, maxroot, keepStore, store, sensErrCon, adjoint, maxOrder and stald; each overrides the batch-wide argument of the same name.

times, parms

Batch-wide times and parms as in solveODE(), for the conditions that do not give their own. Default NULL.

tangent

Optional numeric matrix, the tangent of the inputs; shapes in Details. Default NULL: the identity on the active sensitivities.

hessian

Optional numeric array, the second derivative of the inputs; shapes in Details. Needs a model with attr(model, "deriv2"). Default NULL: the inputs are affine in \(\theta\).

fixed

Optional character vector, sensitivity names held fixed in this call, a subset of attr(model, "dimNames")$sens. Unlike fixed of cppODE() it changes without recompiling. Not with a full or partial tangent. Default NULL.

forcings

Named list of forcing data, one element per name in attr(model, "forcings"): a data.frame with columns time and value, or a two-column matrix. cppODE() and cvode() take the forcing names, this argument the data. A forcing is the monotone cubic Hermite interpolant (PCHIP) of the data points and constant beyond the first and the last point, see forcingValues(). Default NULL.

abstol

Absolute error tolerance. Default 1e-6.

reltol

Relative error tolerance. Default 1e-6.

maxattempts

Maximum number of consecutive step attempts without progress in time before the solve stops with return_code = -4. Default 50.

maxsteps

Maximum total number of integration steps. Default 1e6.

hini

Initial step size; 0 (default) triggers automatic estimation.

roottol

Tolerance for locating root events. Default 1e-6. Under rootfunc = "equilibrate" the solve stops once every \(|\dot x_i| \le \mathrm{roottol}\, |x_i| + \mathrm{abstol}\); on a cppODE() model the test covers the sensitivities as well.

maxroot

Maximum number of triggers per root event. Default 1.

cores

Number of threads, at most the processors; one for a single condition. NULL (default) takes the first of getOption("cppDE.cores"), getOption("Ncpus") and parallel::detectCores(logical = FALSE) that is set. 1 forces the serial loop.

traceFile

Optional. Either one path per condition, or a single path used as a template, in which case the condition's name (or index) is inserted before the extension. Needs a model built with stepTrace = TRUE. Default NULL.

onFailure

Applied once after all conditions have run. "stop" (default) runs every condition, then raises one error naming the failed ones; "warn" and "silent" as in solveODE().

cotangent

The cotangent of the outputs, [n_t, n_x] or [n_t, n_x, n_seed]. Required by a model compiled with derivMode = "reverse" or "forward-reverse" unless keepStore = TRUE; an error on any other model. result$cotangent is then \(\sum_{t,i} w_{t,i}\, \partial x_i(t) / \partial \theta\), one column per seed. Default NULL.

curvature

Optional, "forward-reverse" only: the derivative of cotangent along the tangent, [n_t, n_x, n_seed, n_s]. For a cotangent that is the gradient of a functional of the outputs, this is that functional's Hessian applied to the output tangent. Default NULL: the cotangent is constant in \(\theta\).

keepStore

Logical, default FALSE. Return the checkpoints of a reverse solve as $store, for a later solve to reuse through store. The cotangent may then be omitted, and the solve returns the values alone. Only on a cppODE() model compiled with derivMode = "reverse".

store

The $store of an earlier solve of the same model at the same times and parms. The solve then integrates nothing and runs the backward sweep alone. A store from a different point is an error. A store may be reused any number of times. Default NULL.

sensErrCon

Logical. Include the sensitivities, under derivMode = "forward-reverse" the tangents, in the error test and the first step. Default TRUE; FALSE is cheaper and less accurate, gives the steps and corrector iterations of a value run, so the sensitivities are the derivative of the computed solution and equal those of the reverse mode to rounding, and under "forward-reverse" gives a step grid that does not depend on the directions of the tangent. Needs a model with sensitivities, has no effect under derivMode = "reverse", and a cvode() model takes TRUE only.

adjoint

Optional adjointControl() object for a model compiled with derivMode = "reverse". Default NULL, the same as adjointControl().

maxOrder

Optional upper bound on the order of a multistep method, 1 to 5 for "bdf" and 1 to 12 for "adams". Default NULL, the method's own maximum. An error on "rb4" and "tsit5".

stald

Logical, default FALSE. Stability limit detection for method "bdf": the order drops when the step size leaves the stability region of the current order. See Stepping and error control.

Value

A list of solveODE() results, one per condition, named after conditions, with attribute threads, the thread count used.

Details

Results are bit-identical to the serial path. The batch falls back to a serial loop in a forked child, inside an OpenMP region, or without OpenMP; see batchAvailable(). A model without a batch entry point is solved by solveODE() per condition.

See also

solveODE(); prepareBatch() and solveBatch() for repeated solves of the same conditions; batchAvailable(). Batches of conditions in the Guide.

Examples

# \donttest{
if (codegenAvailable()) {
  ## One model, several conditions, solved on threads in one call. A condition's
  ## list overrides the batch-wide arguments.
  f <- cppODE(c(x = "-k*x"), deriv = FALSE)
  conditions <- list(slow = list(parms = c(x = 1, k = 0.1)),
                     fast = list(parms = c(x = 1, k = 1)))
  res <- solveODEBatch(f, conditions, times = 0:5)
  sapply(res, function(r) r$variable[, "x"])
}
# }
